To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 1B, IC and N genes of human respiratory syncyti virus (RSV), representing two antigenic subgroups, are highly conserved at both the nucleotide and amino acid levels, and that intergenic and non-translative sequences that are not part of the presumed transcriptive signals are much less well consereved than sequences that are part of translational reading frames.
the 1B, IC and N proteins of RSV are highly conserved in antigenic subgroup, and that intergenic regions are much more conserved than non-coding regions of the genes.
the nucleotide and amino acid sequences of RSV 1B, IC and N proteins are highly conserved between antigenic subgroups and that the gene-end signals of these genes are conserved between subtypes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the sequence conservation of the 1B, IC and N genes and proteins between subgroups A and 13 of human respiratory syncytlal virus, and the sequence divergence between the A2 and 18537 strains of subgroup A.
the sequence conservation and divergence between the 1B, IC and N genes of RSV subgroups A and 13, and the sequence conservation between the A2 and Long strains of subgroup A.
the nucleotide sequence conservation and divergence in the 1B, IC and N genes and the intergenic regions between these genes of RSV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N gene and N protein are the most conserved of RSV genes, and that the gene-start and gene-end signals are highly conserved between RSV subgroups A and
the N protein is the most conserved of the RSV proteins.

the 1B, IC and N genes and proteins of human RSV strains of subgroups A and/or B are highly conserved at all levels, and that the intergenic sequences are much less conserved than the coding sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 1B, IC and N proteins of RSV strains of antigenic subroups A and B are highly conserved, and that there is no evidence for major antigenic differences in the N protein between strains of the two subgroups.
the N gene is the most conserved, the 1C gene is the most diverged, and the 1B gene is intermediate.

RSV 1B, IC and N genes are highly conserved in nucleotide and deduce amino acid sequences, that the gene-start and gene-end signals are highly conserved, that intergenic sequences between 1B and IC and between IC and N are less well conserved, that 1B and 1C intergenic regions are highly conserved between RSV antigenic subgroups and that the N gene is highly conserved between subroups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleotide sequences of the 1B, IC and N genes of RSV strains of antigenic subtypes A and B are highly conserved, whereas intergenic and noncoding sequences are more variable.
